blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Charge is retried forever, without backoff, on a non-idempotent call) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Payment call has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts) with exponential backoff and jitter, retry only transient errors (connection errors, timeouts, 5xx/429) and never 4xx such as a declined card, and send an idempotency key derived from order_id so the provider deduplicates a retried charge. After the last attempt, raise an error naming the order and the provider status. Scenario: the provider charges the card but the response is lost or returns 502, so the loop posts the same charge again and the customer is charged twice; a 400/402 is retried every second forever, pinning the checkout worker and hammering the provider during an outage.
findings.title: Charge is retried forever, without backoff, on a non-idempotent call

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit timeout, e.g. timeout=(3, 10) for connect and read. Scenario: the provider accepts the connection but never answers; requests waits indefinitely, the checkout request hangs with no error and no log, and the worker is lost until restarted. Combined with R-ops-1, a read timeout must not lead to a blind re-charge: rely on the idempotency key.
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Log every failed attempt with structured fields (order_id, attempt, HTTP status, exception class, provider error code — never card data or credentials) and the final failure at error level. Scenario: the provider is down or rejects the API call; the operator sees only stuck checkouts, with nothing in the logs to say that the payment provider is failing or for which orders.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL (and any credentials added later) from the environment or the application configuration, so staging and tests can point at the provider's sandbox. Scenario: if the provider has a sandbox endpoint, every environment, staging included, charges against the production endpoint. Confidence low: whether the provider uses distinct endpoints per environment could not be verified.
findings.title: Provider URL hard-coded instead of read from configuration
